title: Questions from the coaches' chat
goal: Stop losing the questions coaches ask in the Teams chat: see every one of them as an object with a status, read the answer if somebody gave one, and answer the open ones from what this tool already knows — with a person reading the wording before it goes back to a room full of colleagues.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: Name the screen and carry the one page-level action: Refresh, which pulls what is new in the chat since the last pull rather than re-reading the copy on disk — the same distinction the two catalogs needed. Beside it, which chat is being watched and when it was last pulled, because a screen that silently watches nothing looks exactly like a chat where nobody asks anything. Changing the chat is a secondary action, not a page: it is done once per install by pasting the Teams 'Copy link'.

zones.name: toolbar
zones.purpose: Everything that narrows the ledger, in one row of equal-height controls: search over the question text and the person who asked; the Open / Answered / All switch carrying its counts, because the default view hides everything already dealt with and a list that silently drops most of itself reads as broken; then one dropdown per facet the classifier assigns — topic (access, tooling, process, people, money, other) and who asked. Search renders EXPANDED. Under the row, on a line of its own: how many are open, how many match, and how old the pull is.

zones.name: content
zones.purpose: One card per question, in the same four blocks every other card in this tool uses. WHO ASKED: the person, when, and the topic as a badge, with the status (open / answered in the chat / answered from here) on the right. WHAT WAS ASKED: the message in their own words, clamped to a few lines, with the link that opens it in Teams — the chat stays the source of truth and this screen never pretends to replace it. THE ANSWER: if somebody already answered in the thread, that answer and who wrote it, because half the value here is that the same question has been answered three times by three people; if nobody has, the draft this tool built from the workbook, the programme rubric and the questions already answered, with the sources it used named under it. A draft with no source says so plainly — 'nothing in our data answers this' is an answer a coordinator can act on, and an invented one is worse than silence. WHAT YOU CAN DO: two icon actions, like the catalogs — copy the answer, or open the send dialog. Nothing else on the card.

zones.name: dialogs
zones.purpose: The one write this screen performs against the outside world, and the one setting it needs. Sending an answer is a Modal showing the exact text that will be posted, editable, with the question quoted above it — the same rule as the coaches' outreach and the weekly check-in: this writes into a room full of colleagues, so nothing is sent that has not been read. Linking the chat is a small form taking the Teams 'Copy link' URL, the same paste the digest app already accepts, because a chat id typed by hand is a support ticket waiting to happen.

states.loading: Six Skeleton shape=block cards under a single aria-busy on the grid. Reading the ledger is a local file; the PULL is a network call and shows as a loading button rather than as an empty screen, so the questions already on the machine stay readable while new ones arrive.
states.empty: EmptyState through the template's empty prop, three cases kept apart because they need different actions: reason='no-data' with icon=chat when no chat has been linked yet, offering the paste; reason='no-data' with icon=check when the chat is linked and every question is answered — the good state, and it says so rather than looking broken; reason='no-matches' with icon=tune when the filters emptied the list, offering to clear them.
states.error: Alert tone=danger above the list, with the reason and a retry. Three failures worth telling apart in words: Microsoft sign-in expired (offer the sign-in), the local server is not running (offer nothing but say what to start), and the chat could not be read because the account is not a member of it. An unread chat is not a chat with no questions.
states.noPermission: Alert tone=info in place of the list when the signed-in account is not a member of the watched chat. The chat is read with the coach's own Microsoft session, so whoever can open it in Teams can read it here and nobody else can — this states that rather than implying a permission system the app does not have, and offers the sign-in and the paste-another-chat action.

data: the watched chat: coach/questions/chat.json — chat id, topic and the watermark of the last pull. Set once from a Teams 'Copy link' URL (the id is the 19:...@thread.v2 segment), the same paste apps/teams-digest already accepts. Never hardcoded: one install watches one chat, and which chat that is belongs to the instance.

messages: pulled with the signed-in coach's own token through packages/msgraph (auth.mjs + chat.mjs), only what is newer than the watermark. The same reader and the same watermark rule the digest app is built on, so a chat with two years of history does not arrive as two years of unread.

the ledger: coach/questions/questions.jsonl, append-only, one object per line — message id, who asked, when, the text, the Teams permalink, the topic, the status, the answer if there is one, who answered and when. Append-only for the reason the roster events are: the history of what was asked and answered is the artefact, and a rewritten file cannot be trusted.

classification and drafting: one pass through the coach's own CLI via the local bridge (tools/lib/cli.mjs, the same transport the vetting and check-in functions use). It decides what is a question, what topic it belongs to, whether a later message answered it, and drafts an answer for the open ones. No model call leaves this machine except through that CLI.

what an answer is drafted FROM, in this order: the questions already answered in this ledger (the same question asked twice should not get two different answers), the workbook (coach/sources/*.json), the programme rubric (data/program.json), and the repository's own docs. Each draft carries the sources it used; a draft with none says so.
openQuestions: Whether the org side wants this ledger published back to them — a repeated question with a good answer is a FAQ the programme leads should own, and today it would live on one coordinator's machine. The file is append-only and in the shape a shared folder could read, so turning that on is a transport change, not a data change.

How reliably a reply can be tied to the question it answers. Teams threads make it explicit; a reply typed into the main flow does not, and the classifier will have to guess from wording and timing. The screen shows what it decided and lets a person correct the status, so a wrong guess is visible and fixable rather than silent.

Whether the same screen should let a coordinator answer a question that nobody asked in the chat yet — writing the FAQ ahead of time. Deliberately out of the first slice: the value here is the questions that already exist and go unanswered.

behaviours.given: a question lifted from the coaches' chat and answered on the board
behaviours.then: the question keeps its status instead of reappearing as new
behaviours.why: The screen's whole point: stop losing questions — which includes not resurrecting the answered ones.
behaviours.pendingReason: The questions store has no test harness yet; the test lands with the store's first suite, named coach-questions#question-keeps-its-status.
